frequency_question: What proportion of major executive tariff or import restriction actions are fully implemented and operational within 120 days of initial announcement?
membership_rule: Includes all instances where a U.S. President announced sweeping country- or sector-specific tariff measures outside standard legislative timelines; excludes minor technical amendments and routine antidumping/countervailing duty adjustments.
coverage_note: 4 major historical precedents identified; universe of rapid executive trade interventions is small.
known_gaps: Border integration for automotive supply chains involves complex rules of origin verification that typically require longer lead times than steel or general imports.
skeleton: Historical instances of unilateral executive tariff announcements executed via emergency powers or statutory delegation, evaluated for whether operational rules took effect within roughly 4 months.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 historical comparable precedents
validity_reason: Administrative procedures and statutory emergency trade powers (like IEEPA or Section 232/301) remain stable across this timeframe.
